# Additions to Daniel Chapter 3 (Bel and the Dragon) — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus (Theodotion recension), Additions to Daniel 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADD_003_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition 3: Two episodes — Daniel as idol-buster and dragon-killer. The tone is satirical, even comic. Daniel laughs twice (vv. 7, 18). The Habakkuk episode (vv. 32–38) is pure wonder-tale. Keep the wit.]*

**1** Astyages died and was gathered to his ancestors. Cyrus the Persian took the throne.

**2** Daniel was a personal companion of the king — more honored than any of his other friends.

**3** The Babylonians had an idol called Bel. Every single day it consumed twelve huge measures of fine flour, forty sheep, and six jars of wine.

**4** The king revered Bel and went to worship him every day. Daniel, meanwhile, worshiped his own God.

**5** The king asked him: "Why don't you worship Bel?" Daniel answered: "Because I don't worship idols made by human hands. I worship the living God — the one who created heaven and earth and rules over all living things."

**6** "But doesn't it seem obvious to you," said the king, "that Bel is alive? Look how much he eats and drinks every single day!"

**7** Daniel laughed. "Don't be fooled, your majesty. Inside that thing is clay. Outside is bronze. It has never eaten or drunk a single thing."

**8** The king turned red with anger and called for his priests. "Tell me who is eating all this food," he said, "or you will die.

**9** But if you prove that Bel eats it — Daniel dies. He has blasphemed against Bel." Daniel said: "Fine. Let it be that way."

**10** There were seventy priests of Bel, not counting their wives and children. The king went with Daniel into Bel's temple.

**11** The priests said: "We'll leave, your majesty. You set out the food yourself, mix the wine, seal the doors. Come back tomorrow morning. If Bel hasn't eaten everything — we die. If he has, Daniel dies, because he lied."

**12** They weren't worried. Underneath the table there was a concealed entrance. They used it to sneak in every night and eat everything.

**13** After the priests left, the king set the food out before Bel. Then Daniel told his servants to bring ashes. They scattered them all over the temple floor — just the king watching. Then they went out and sealed the door.

**14** That night the priests came in exactly as they always did — wives, children, everyone — and ate and drank until it was all gone.

**15** The king got up early the next morning. Daniel was with him.

**16** "Daniel," said the king, "are the seals still intact?" "Still intact, your majesty."

**17** The doors opened. The king looked at the table. He let out a shout: "Bel is great! There is no deception in him at all!"

**18** Daniel laughed again. He caught the king before he could go in and said: "Look down. Look at the floor. Whose footprints are those?"

**19** The king looked. "Men's footprints. Women's. Children's." His face went dark with rage.

**20** He seized the priests — and their wives and children with them. They showed him the secret entrance under the table, the one they always used to get in and eat everything.

**21** The king had them all executed. Then he handed Bel over to Daniel, who smashed it to pieces along with its temple.

**22** Now there was also a great dragon in that place, and the Babylonians worshiped it as a god.

**23** The king said to Daniel: "You can't say this one isn't alive. Worship the dragon."

**24** "I worship the Lord my God," Daniel said. "He is the only living God.

**25** Give me permission, your majesty, and I'll kill the dragon — no sword, no weapon." The king said: "Permission granted."

**26** Daniel took pitch and fat and hair and cooked them down together into balls. He pushed them down the dragon's throat. The dragon swallowed them — and exploded. "There," Daniel said. "That's what you were worshiping."

**27** When the Babylonians heard what had happened, they were enraged. They came together against the king: "He's gone over to the Jews. He tore down Bel, he killed the dragon, he had the priests killed."

**28** They came to the king and said: "Give us Daniel or we kill you and your whole house."

**29** The king looked at them pressing in on every side. He had no choice. He handed Daniel over.

**30** They threw him into the lions' den. He was there for six days.

**31** Seven lions were in the den. Every day they had been given two human bodies and two sheep. Now they were given nothing — to make sure they would be hungry enough to eat Daniel.

**32** Back in Judea, the prophet Habakkuk had made a stew. He had crumbled some bread into a bowl. He was about to walk it out to the field workers.

**33** An angel of the Lord appeared to him and said: "Take that food to Babylon. To Daniel. He's in the lions' den."

**34** Habakkuk said: "I've never been to Babylon. I have no idea where the lions' den is."

**35** The angel of the Lord grabbed him by the top of his head and picked him up by the hair. A blast of wind — and Habakkuk was in Babylon, hovering right above the den.

**36** He called down: "Daniel! Daniel! God sent you a meal!"

**37** Daniel called back: "You remembered me, God. You never abandon those who love you."

**38** He sat up and ate. Immediately the angel carried Habakkuk back home.

**39** On the seventh day the king came, grieving, to the den. He looked in — and there was Daniel. Sitting there. Perfectly fine.

**40** The king shouted at the top of his voice: "Lord God of Daniel — you are great! There is no god but you!"

**41** He pulled Daniel out. The men who had tried to destroy him — he threw them into the den. They were devoured on the spot, right in front of him.

**42** Then the king proclaimed: "Let everyone in the whole world fear the God of Daniel. He is the Savior. He works signs and wonders on earth. He has delivered Daniel from the lions."
